S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

info.persona: Tonya Kincaid, a 33‑year‑old DIY‑savvy painter, balances structured project planning with a laid‑back love for eco‑friendly finishes, garden‑to‑table meals, historic novels, and a habit of delaying paperwork for a weekend concert.
info.professional_persona: Tonya Kincaid, a seasoned residential painter and paper‑hanging specialist in Saint Louis, combines precise blueprint reading, eco‑friendly paint expertise, and a talent for estimating material needs to manage client projects with structured timelines while mentoring apprentices as she works toward certified lead‑painter status and her own sustainable finish business.
info.cultural_background: Tonya grew up in a middle-class, white Midwestern family in St. Louis County, experiencing the region’s emphasis on community, reliability, and practicality. Her heritage includes German and Irish ancestry common to the area, and she was raised with values of hard work, modesty, and neighborly friendliness. She attended local public schools and some college courses at a community college, where she began learning trade skills. The cultural environment of the Midwest’s blend of urban and suburban life informs her pragmatic approach to work, her cooperative nature, and her appreciation for straightforward communication.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time Tonya enjoys hands-on DIY home projects, such as building simple furniture or refreshing rooms with her own paint. She practices acrylic painting as a personal artistic outlet, tends to a small vegetable garden, and hikes the nearby Ozark trails. She is an avid reader of historical fiction, attends local live-music shows, volunteers with Habitat for Humanity on weekend build days, and occasionally practices yoga to maintain balance.
info.sports_persona: Tonya Kincaid enjoys weekend hikes on the Ozark Trail as a member of the Saint Louis Outdoor Club, follows the Saint Louis Cardinals baseball and Saint Louis Blues hockey teams, occasionally runs a 5 K in local charity events, and participates in a community yoga class to maintain flexibility.
info.arts_persona: Tonya Kincaid channels her creative side through acrylic painting inspired by the vibrant colors of local street murals, devours historical fiction by Philippa Gregory and Ken Follett, and regularly attends live‑music shows at BB's Jazz Club featuring artists like Nathaniel Rateliff and The Avett Brothers, while also visiting the Saint Louis Art Museum for inspiration.
info.travel_persona: Tonya Kincaid prefers short, budget‑friendly road trips that blend planned stops with spontaneous detours, has explored Nashville’s music scene and Branson’s theme parks, dreams of a sustainable‑focused tour of Portland and the Pacific Northwest, and hopes to one day wander Tuscany’s vineyards for garden and culinary inspiration.
info.culinary_persona: Tonya Kincaid enjoys cooking with garden‑fresh heirloom tomatoes, zucchini, basil, and rosemary, skillfully prepares roasted vegetable quinoa bowls, herb‑roasted chicken, and homemade strawberry shortcake, dabbles in grilling salmon with lemon‑dill sauce, and occasionally treats herself to Saint Louis BBQ at Pappy’s Smokehouse while sipping a local craft brew.

info.persona: Steven Johnson channels a blend of meticulous curiosity and social energy into every rev of the Mustang, yet their habit of over‑committing to projects often leaves them juggling late‑night work, stress‑filled spreadsheets, and a constant stash of spare parts on the kitchen counter.
info.professional_persona: Steven Johnson, a seasoned ASE‑certified automotive technician with over two decades of hands‑on expertise in engine performance, brakes, electrical systems, and hybrid powertrains, blends his practical curiosity and organized yet flexible workflow to mentor apprentices, streamline workshop operations, and pursue a master‑technician credential as he plans to open a high‑performance EV repair shop and teach at the community college.
info.cultural_background: Steven grew up in a blue‑collar, middle‑class family in Northampton County, Pennsylvania, with deep roots in the region’s industrial and agricultural heritage. His ancestry includes German and Irish lineage, and he was raised within the cultural norms of the Lehigh Valley—hard work, self‑reliance, and close‑knit community involvement. Local traditions such as high‑school football, church gatherings, neighborhood car clubs, and a shared love for automobiles have shaped his work ethic, social life, and sense of responsibility toward family and community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: On weekends Steven enjoys restoring a 1967 Mustang, attending local car shows and meet‑ups, playing in a community basketball league, fishing at Lake Nockamixon, tackling DIY home‑improvement projects, grilling barbecue for friends and family, and volunteering at the community center to teach basic car maintenance. He relaxes by listening to classic rock and watching racing events on television.
info.sports_persona: Steven Johnson stays active in a weekday evening community basketball league affiliated with the local YMCA, roots for the Philadelphia 76ers and the Eagles during NFL and NBA seasons, spends spring and summer mornings casting at Lake Nockamixon, and complements his on‑court cardio with occasional home‑gym strength sessions, viewing fitness as a social outlet rather than a solitary grind.
info.arts_persona: Steven Johnson, a classic‑rock aficionado who riffs on Led Zeppelin, AC DC, and The Rolling Stones while tinkering in the garage, also enjoys the cinematic thrill of “Bullitt” and “The Fast and the Furious” series, occasionally visits the Philadelphia Museum of Art for modern exhibits, and captures his restored Mustang in black‑and‑white photography, letting music and visual art fuel his creative spark.
info.travel_persona: Steven Johnson prefers well‑planned road‑trip adventures that combine his love for classic cars with family time, such as weekend drives to the Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, a recent pilgrimage to the Porsche Museum in Stuttgart, and annual summer escapes to the Blue Ridge Parkway, always budgeting travel around work and school commitments while hunting for new Mustang memorabilia.
info.culinary_persona: Steven Johnson, a confident grillmaster, regularly whips up Texas‑style smoked brisket, Kansas City burnt ends, and char‑grilled trout fresh from Lake Nockamixon using hickory chips, dry rubs of brown sugar and smoked paprika, and pairs the feast with craft IPAs, while also enjoying a well‑executed classic cheeseburger on a Sunday family barbecue.

info.persona: Yen Shih, a methodical yet quirky master carpenter, they fuse Asian‑inspired joinery with Texan design, mentor apprentices over coffee, practice tai chi at sunrise, and occasionally hoard vintage hand tools that clutter a carefully organized workshop.
info.professional_persona: Yen Shih, a veteran carpenter with over three decades of experience, they blend meticulous blueprint reading, CNC routing, and traditional joinery with a curious eye for design, while their organized, reliable nature ensures projects finish on schedule and their sociable, mentoring style fosters a collaborative workshop environment.
info.cultural_background: Born to immigrant parents from Taiwan, Yen grew up in a household that valued craftsmanship, discipline, and respect for tradition. Her family’s reverence for woodwork—particularly intricate joinery and ornamental carving—shaped her early fascination with building and art. While fully integrated into Houston’s multicultural landscape, she maintains a strong connection to East Asian cultural practices such as tea ceremony, lunar‑calendar celebrations, and community gatherings at local Asian cultural centers. This bicultural perspective informs her design aesthetic, blending minimalist Asian motifs with the eclectic, vibrant spirit of Texas.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Yen enjoys exploring Houston’s vibrant art scene, attending museum exhibitions and local galleries. She paints watercolors, practices calligraphy, and captures architectural details through photography. Her love for gardening provides inspiration for organic designs, while cooking traditional East Asian dishes connects her to her heritage. Yen participates in tai chi classes for mindfulness, volunteers at community renovation projects, and regularly joins woodworking meet‑ups and cultural festivals throughout the city.
info.sports_persona: Yen Shih, an avid supporter of the Houston Astros and Rockets, they incorporate early‑morning jogs along Buffalo Bayou and weekly tai chi circles into their fitness routine, enjoy seasonal pickleball at the local community center, and join a casual woodworking‑and‑cycling club that meets for weekend rides.
info.arts_persona: Yen Shih, who spends weekends wandering the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston and sketching architectural details for watercolor studies, they draw inspiration from Claude Monet’s impressionist palette, Ai Weiwei’s conceptual installations, and local graffiti artist Rox, integrating these influences into handcrafted furniture and calligraphy practice.
info.travel_persona: Yen Shih, whose travel style blends meticulous planning with spontaneous curiosity, they have explored the historic temples of Kyoto, savored the vineyards of Napa Valley, and frequently retreat to Galveston’s shoreline for weekend inspiration, all while budgeting carefully to fund future trips to the cedar forests of Oregon for timber sourcing research.
info.culinary_persona: Yen Shih, a passionate home cook, they perfect dishes like hand‑rolled dumplings, fragrant pho broth, and char‑siu pork while also embracing Texas staples such as smoked brisket and jalapeño‑infused cornbread, experimenting with fresh herbs from their garden and savoring the balance of umami and smoky flavors.
